name: Band Wigman Franks

abilities.name: Barbarian Testudo
abilities.text: The troops of this unit raise their shields above their heads in a static defensive formation.

abilities.name: Spear Wall
abilities.text: The unit moves into close wall formation.

abilities.name: Square
abilities.text: The unit moves into a close square formation. Note that it cannot move whilst this ability is active.

abilities.name: Shield Screen
abilities.text: The unit raises their shields in a static defensive formation.

abilities.name: Frenzied Charge
abilities.text: Increases the effectiveness of the unit's charge for an extended period.

attributes.name: Snipe
attributes.text: This unit remains hidden while firing.

attributes.name: Guerrilla Deployment
attributes.text: This unit can deploy outside of the deployment zone.

attributes.name: Hide (scrub & forest)
attributes.text: This unit can hide in scrub and forest until enemy units get too close.

attributes.name: Immune to Fear
attributes.text: This unit is immune to the fear effects of scary units.

attributes.name: Impetuous
attributes.text: This unit gets an extra morale bonus when eager.

attributes.name: Disciplined
attributes.text: This unit does not suffer a morale penalty when the general dies. It can also rally after routing more often.

short: Band Wigman Franks, from Old Norse vig-maar "warrior, champion", Old English wiℨ-mann "man of war, soldier", Old Saxon wig-man "warrior, champion", Old High German wig-man identical. Root from ON.vig, OE wiℨ ‘fight, battle’ or ON vígja "to consecrate", OFris wiga identical.
history: Amongst the Franks the term 'heerbann' was used to describe freemen called to bear arms for their country on a contractual basis, rather like the Anglo-Saxon 'fyrd' who came after them. Months prior to embarking on a military campaign the Franks mustered a heerbann, allowing time for them to equip, assemble and train for the conflict ahead. Ignoring a call to join could lead to harsh penalties, although heeding it also had its downsides, as many minor landowners struggled to afford their own armour and weapons. Although changed by the advent of the feudal system, the custom of calling a heerbann remained in place until around the time of the Crusades, gradually evolving into the Medieval French word 'arriere-ban'.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
